source.title: Using Under-Trained Deep Ensembles to Learn Under Extreme Label Noise: A Case Study for Sleep Apnea Detection
source.authors: K. Nikolaidis; T. Plagemann; Stein Kristiansen; Vera Goebel; Mohan Kankanhalli

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates CNN generalization under several levels and types of label corruption, a related test of noisy-label behavior. It does not measure whether training error reaches zero.
record.gate_note: The paper reports clean-test performance for baseline CNNs trained on corrupted labels. It does not report training error on corrupted labels, test error at chance for fully random labels, fitting time, or the claimed fitting behavior on unstructured inputs. EPD results are omitted because they report the study's proposed method rather than what the claim's standard networks do. Results cited from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Baseline CNN results test V4's clean-test degradation component in digit and sensor classification. The authors also report initially high baseline test performance followed by deterioration during training, bearing indirectly on V6. Perfect training fit and direct memorization of noisy labels are not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that properly parametrized EPD improves learning under severe label noise across digit classification and sleep-apnea detection, while consistent wrong-class biases can defeat its under-training strategy.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes under-trained ensembles and evaluation-probability distillation for learning with corrupted labels; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with dataset, corruption type and corruption level; the authors also report that EPD depends on suitable parametrization and can fail under systematic wrong-class bias.
record.problems: The study does not report training error on corrupted labels, so it cannot establish that the baseline fits those labels perfectly. Sleep-apnea datasets are randomly shuffled and split because they have no predefined test sets. Reported uncertainties are standard errors of the mean.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted EPD performance values throughout Tables 1–2 and the realistic-corruption experiments because these quantify the paper's proposed method rather than the claim's standard networks. Figure-only performance curves were also omitted; tabulated baseline values were retained.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training settings.
Time to fit random versus real labels and convergence time across corruption fractions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout corruption levels and the completely random-label endpoint. Sensor results report kappa rather than test error.
Controlled effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and clean-label generalization.
Separate training trajectories for correctly and incorrectly labelled samples, and direct demonstration that later learning fits noisy labels.

missing.what: Baseline learning trajectories relevant to V6: initially high clean-test performance followed by an early decline on SVHN and NAF:AE at Pair-0.45. Add qualitative rows distinguishing this indirect evidence from measured noisy-label memorization; exact curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.
missing.locator: Randomized Corruption, Digit Classification and Sleep Apnea Detection; Figure 3(c–d)

record.verdict_notes: T3 reflects results extending the claim to sensor classification alongside digit experiments. Missing training-fit measurements do not warrant limits_scope. Remove the record's Sym.-0.63 limits_scope verdict. Figure-only results were broadly declared omitted, but the V6 trajectories need rows to represent this separately tested component. The Figure 3 caption and surrounding prose disagree on panel assignments; dataset and condition identify the findings.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks reach zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, and their test error in that setting.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence as corrupted-label fraction increases.
Fitting shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Whether training error remains perfect at each corruption level; the study reports clean-test performance only and does not test corruption all the way to 100%.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent fitting random labels or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels during training.
